newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese government and opposition unite on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese government and opposition unite on EMU.

text.p: Portugal's Socialist government and its main opposition staged a rare show of unity on Wednesday, agreeing a joint motion to parliament backing the country's bid to join European economic and monetary union (EMU) in the first wave in 1999.

The motion will be put to parliament, where the two parties hold a combined 85 percent of the seats, in a debate on Thursday in which Prime Minister Antonio Guterres and Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco will take part.
The government has made qualifying for EMU at the first attempt its top priority, drawing up a deficit-cutting budget for 1997 and holding down salary rises to contain inflation.

The opposition Social Democrat Party (PSD), a centre-right party, shares the government's commitment to EMU but it has previously preferred to abstain in parliamentary votes on the budget and other issues related to monetary union.

Monetary union is "not an issue for political combat between the government and opposition, it is a question of national interest," said PSD parliamentary leader Luis Marques Mendes after the decision to table the joint motion.

Portugal has reacted angrily to suggestions by some northern European political and business leaders that the so-called 'Club Med' countries -- Spain, Italy and Portugal -- should opt to wait rather than join EMU at the start even if they meet the stiff entry qualifications.
The government has repeatedly said that if Portugal passes the economic entry tests, covering such areas as budget deficits, inflation and national debt levels, then it will join at the start.

"Entry into the euro (the single currency) at the start, is a strategic objective and fundamental to our future as a nation at the heart of the European design," said Joaquim Pina Moura, secretary of state at the Prime Minister's office, on Wednesday.
Economic analysts say Portugal has a good chance of meeting EMU entry targets, and local interest rates have fallen sharply in past months as investors bet on its being included.
